text: So I appeal to the elders among you, as a fellow elder and a witness of Christ's sufferings, and one who also shares in the glory that is about to be revealed:
shepherd the flock of God that is among you, watching over it not under compulsion but willingly, as God would have it; not for shameful gain but eagerly;
not lording it over those entrusted to your care, but being examples to the flock.

versions.text: not lording it over those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.
versions.explanation: τῶν κλήρων refers to the portions of the flock allotted to each elder's charge; 'entrusted to your care' makes the sense clearer without adding length. A footnote noting the literal sense ('those allotted to you') could also be helpful.

text: And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you will receive the unfading crown of glory.
In the same way, you who are younger, submit to the elders. And all of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble."
Humble yourselves, then, under God's mighty hand, so that he may lift you up in due time,
casting all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.
Be sober; be watchful. Your adversary the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour.
Resist him, firm in the faith, knowing that your brothers and sisters throughout the world are undergoing the same kind of suffering.
And after you have suffered a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory in Christ, will himself restore you, support you, strengthen you, and establish you.

versions.text: And after you have suffered a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory in Christ, will himself restore you, make you strong, firm, and steadfast.
versions.explanation: The Greek piles up four distinct future verbs (καταρτίσει, στηρίξει, σθενώσει, θεμελιώσει). The current rendering compresses three of them into a string of adjectives ('strong, firm, and steadfast'), weakening the accumulating rhythm and losing the verbal force. Four parallel verbs also read well aloud.

text: To him be the power forever and ever. Amen.

versions.text: To him be the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
versions.explanation: 'the dominion' with the definite article is stilted in English doxology; κράτος here denotes might or power. Dropping the article gives a smoother spoken cadence.

text: With the help of Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly, encouraging you and testifying that this is the true grace of God. Stand fast in it.
She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you greetings, and so does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.
